# Knowledge base

Drop **de-identified** clinical guidelines here (`.md`, `.txt`, `.csv`, `.json`).

- `seed/` — built-in emergency pathways (included by default)
- Add hospital protocols as PDF → convert to `.md` or upload via your pipeline

After adding files, redeploy (build runs `npm run ingest`) or call:

`POST /api/knowledge/reindex` with header `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ADMIN_SECRET` if set.

Semantic search activates when `OPENAI_API_KEY` is present at ingest time.

# Canada — training mode reference (not clinical clearance)

This app runs in **training/simulation mode** for Canada. Verify all content against current Canadian sources before any future clinical use.

## Regulatory context (high level)
- **Health Canada** regulates software as a medical device when intended for diagnosis/treatment decisions.
- **PIPEDA** (federal) and provincial laws (e.g. **PHIPA** in Ontario, **HIA** in Alberta) govern personal health information.
- **CPSO / provincial colleges** set practice standards for physicians; trainees work under supervision.

## Canadian guideline sources to add (upload to knowledge/)
- Health Canada publications
- Canadian Thoracic Society / Canadian Cardiovascular Society guidelines
- Choosing Wisely Canada
- Provincial emergency department standards (e.g. Ontario MOH)
- UpToDate is licensed — do not scrape; use institution subscriptions separately

## Training case conventions
- Use fictitious names: "Patient A", "58M trainee case 12"
- No real health card numbers (OHIP, RAMQ, PHN, etc.)
- Document learning objectives: "rule out PE", "practice sepsis workup"

real health card numbers (OHIP, RAMQ, PHN, etc.)
- Document learning objectives: "rule out PE", "practice sepsis workup"

## Cannot-miss (same clinical principles, local pathways differ)
Apply the same emergency screening as global seed content, but disposition and investigations must follow local Canadian hospital protocols when in supervised clinical training — never via this uncertified app on real patients.

# Cannot-miss diagnoses (emergency screening)

Licensed physicians must rule out these before anchoring on benign causes. Local protocols override this list.

## Chest pain
- Acute coronary syndrome (STEMI/NSTEMI)
- Aortic dissection
- Pulmonary embolism
- Tension pneumothorax
- Esophageal rupture (Boerhaave)

**Red flags:** tearing pain to back, hypotension, unequal pulses, new murmur, SpO₂ drop, hemoptysis, syncope.

## Headache
- Subarachnoid hemorrhage
- Meningitis / encephalitis
- Intracranial hemorrhage / mass
- Cervical artery dissection
- Acute angle-closure glaucoma
- Cavernous sinus thrombosis

**Red flags:** thunderclap onset, fever + neck stiffness, focal neuro deficit, papilledema, postpartum, anticoagulation, immunocompromised.

derclap onset, fever + neck stiffness, focal neuro deficit, papilledema, postpartum, anticoagulation, immunocompromised.

## Abdominal pain
- Ruptured ectopic pregnancy
- Mesenteric ischemia
- Ruptured AAA
- Bowel obstruction / perforation
- Acute pancreatitis (severe)
- Testicular/ovarian torsion

**Red flags:** peritonitis, GI bleeding, pregnancy, age >50 with new pain, AF on anticoagulation, disproportionate pain vs exam.

## Fever without clear source
- Sepsis / septic shock
- Meningococcemia
- Endocarditis
- Deep space infection (epidural, nec fasc)
- Malaria (travel history)

## Shortness of breath
- PE, pneumothorax, anaphylaxis, ACS, status asthmaticus, ARDS, methemoglobinemia

## Syncope
- Arrhythmia, PE, aortic stenosis, SAH, GI bleed, ectopic rupture

## Syncope
- Arrhythmia, PE, aortic stenosis, SAH, GI bleed, ectopic rupture

## General actions when red flag present
1. Stabilize ABCs and vitals
2. Do not delay time-critical tests (ECG, lactate, pregnancy test, CT as indicated)
3. Escalate per local sepsis / stroke / MI / PE pathways

# Chest pain — rapid assessment pathway

## Within 10 minutes
- ABCs, vitals, SpO₂, IV access if unstable
- **12-lead ECG** — if STEMI, activate reperfusion pathway per local protocol
- Aspirin (if not contraindicated) when ACS suspected
- Brief HPI: onset, character, radiation, exertional, pleuritic, positional

## Differential by likelihood (pre-test — refine with data)
**Life-threatening first**
1. ACS / unstable angina
2. Pulmonary embolism
3. Aortic dissection
4. Tension pneumothorax
5. Esophageal rupture

**Other common**
- Pericarditis, myocarditis
- Pneumonia, pleurisy
- GERD / spasm (diagnosis of exclusion in ED)

## Useful tests
- Troponin (serial per protocol), D-dimer only with appropriate pre-test probability for PE
- CXR
- CT angiography: PE protocol or aortic dissection when suspicion high

## PE red flags
Sudden dyspnea, pleuritic pain, hemoptysis, recent immobilization/surgery, OCP, cancer, unilateral leg swelling, tachycardia out of proportion.

## Dissection red flags
Tearing pain to back, pulse/BP differential, new diastolic murmur, neurologic deficits, widened mediastinum on CXR.

## Documentation
Record explicit ruled-out cannot-miss conditions when dispositioning home.

# Fever — structured workup (adult, CDS reference)

## Immediate history
- Onset, pattern, travel, sick contacts, animal exposure
- Immunosuppression, splenectomy, pregnancy, devices (lines, prosthetics)
- Focused review: respiratory, urinary, abdominal, skin/soft tissue, CNS

## Examination priorities
- Full vitals including orthostatics if tolerated
- Skin (petechiae, cellulitis), HEENT, lungs, abdomen, GU if indicated
- Neurologic if altered or headache

## Initial tests (adapt locally)
- CBC, CMP, lactate
- Blood cultures ×2 before antibiotics if sepsis suspected
- Urinalysis / urine culture
- Chest X-ray if respiratory symptoms
- Pregnancy test when applicable

## High-risk patterns
| Pattern | Consider |
|---------|----------|
| Petechial rash + fever | Meningococcemia — immediate antibiotics |
| Post-procedure / line fever | Line infection, endocarditis |
| RLQ pain + fever | Appendicitis, PID, diverticulitis |
| Flank pain + fever | Pyelonephritis, stone with infection |
| Jaundice + fever | Cholangitis (Charcot triad) |
| Immunocompromised + fever | Broad differential; low threshold for admit |

## Antibiotic stewardship
Match spectrum to focus; reassess at 48–72h with cultures. Document source control needs (drainage, removal of infected hardware).

## Citations to verify locally
WHO sepsis guidance; Surviving Sepsis Campaign (latest edition); IDSA fever and neutropenia guidelines where applicable.
